key_insight: Front-peaked tool–workpiece contact pressure best explains bobbin tool friction stir welding behavior, including hotter material on the retreating side caused by flow from the advancing side.
engineering_relevance: Accurate contact-pressure modeling can improve predictions of weld temperature, plastic deformation, and material transport to support process optimization.
method: Developed a fully coupled thermo-mechanical-fluid CFD model.
Compared front-peaked, uniform, and rear-peaked contact-pressure distributions.
Analyzed temperature fields, deformation-zone shape, and horizontal and vertical material flow.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports superior predictive accuracy for the front-peaked model and experimental agreement that the retreating side is hotter than the advancing side, but provides no quantitative error metrics.
watch_item: Transferability of the front-peaked pressure model across materials, tool geometries, and welding conditions requires further validation.
paper_title: Spatial characteristic of temperature distribution and material flow behaviors during bobbin tool friction stir welding: a computational fluid dynamics study
